rules: Searched every PubMed record in Europe PMC with vitamin C (vitamin C, ascorbic acid, ascorbate) in its title or abstract; downloaded all reviews, randomised trials and guidelines.
Left out animal studies (MeSH tags, or the title when there are none) and retracted papers.
An outcome counts when its words are in the title.

Reviews: meta-analyses or systematic reviews of randomised trials of giving vitamin C, with vitamin C in the title, or in the abstract of a review of several supplements (not reviews of blood levels in observational studies; reviews without an abstract are kept for screening), and not about another group of people (such as sepsis, intensive care or surgery; each outcome's list is in the search definition). Chosen: the three newest meta-analyses (systematic reviews only if fewer than three), plus the most comprehensive one (most trials pooled, read from the abstract). Citations are shown but do not choose.
Newer large trials: randomised trials of at least 1,000 people (read from the abstract) from the year of the newest chosen review on, which those reviews may not include.

Screening: each eligible review's title and abstract was read against the finding's question (who, what was given, compared with what, what was measured) by Claude Code (opus), titles and abstracts only. Only reviews that answer it can be chosen; the others are listed with the reason. The decisions are kept in the repository and have not yet been checked by a clinician.
Overlap: the chosen reviews' reference lists (from Europe PMC) matched against the downloaded vitamin C trials, measured as the corrected covered area (Pieper 2014, PMID 24581293).

left.title: Effects of Vitamin C and/or E Supplementation on Glycemic Control and Cardiovascular Risk Factors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Subgroup Meta-analysis
left.reason: Two parts differ: the people all have type 2 diabetes, and the outcomes are blood sugar, lipids and blood pressure rather than heart disease, cancer or death.

left.title: Letter to the Editor: Comment on "The association between vitamin C and breast cancer, prostate cancer and colorectal cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis"
left.reason: This is a letter to the editor about another review, not a systematic review, and it has no abstract to check against the question.

left.title: Effects of antioxidants on oxidative stress in adult patients with coronary artery disease: A systematic review
left.reason: The people have coronary artery disease, the antioxidants are mostly not vitamin C, and the outcomes are oxidative stress markers.

left.title: From A to E: Uniting vitamins against stroke risk-A systematic review and network meta-analysis
left.reason: Vitamin C is compared with placebo, but the outcome is stroke rather than heart disease, and randomised trials are pooled together with cohort studies.

left.title: The Use of Antioxidants for Cardiovascular Protection in Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review
left.reason: Mostly preclinical studies of antioxidants given during pregnancy for fetal growth restriction, not vitamin C supplements in adults to prevent disease or death.

left.title: Vitamin and Mineral Supplements for the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease and Cancer: Updated Evidence Report and Systematic Review for the US Preventive Services Task Force
left.reason: Randomised trials in healthy adults covering heart disease, cancer and death, but the abstract gives no separate result for vitamin C.

left.title: Circulating vitamin C concentration and risk of cancers: a Mendelian randomization study
left.reason: Mainly a Mendelian randomisation study; its meta-analysis of vitamin C and cancer pools cohort studies with randomised trials.

left.title: Post-Diagnosis use of Antioxidant Vitamin Supplements and Breast Cancer Prognosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
left.reason: The people are breast cancer patients, the studies are observational, and it looks at survival after diagnosis rather than prevention.

left.title: Effects of Vitamin C Supplementation on Glycemic Control and Cardiovascular Risk Factors in People With Type 2 Diabetes: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
left.reason: Two parts differ: the people have type 2 diabetes, and the outcomes are blood markers and blood pressure rather than heart disease, cancer or death.

left.title: Dietary Supplement Use after Cancer Diagnosis in Relation to Total Mortality, Cancer Mortality and Recurrence: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
left.reason: The people are cancer survivors, and the vitamin C results come only from observational studies.

left.title: Vitamin C for Cardiac Protection during Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
left.reason: Vitamin C is given into a vein around a heart procedure (PCI), and the outcomes are mostly markers of heart injury.

left.title: Limited evidence for a beneficial effect of vitamin C supplementation on biomarkers of cardiovascular diseases: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses
left.reason: Vitamin C supplements are studied, but the outcomes are only heart disease risk markers such as blood pressure and lipids, not actual disease.

left.title: The Effect of Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) in the Treatment of Patients with Cancer: A Systematic Review
left.reason: This is about treating people who already have cancer with vitamin C, and few of the included studies are randomised.

left.title: Vitamin C and Heart Health: A Review Based on Findings from Epidemiologic Studies
left.reason: Looks at vitamin C and heart disease, but mixes trial and cohort evidence and does not appear to pool the randomised trials.

left.title: Dietary supplements and risk of cause-specific death, cardiovascular disease, and cancer: a protocol for a systematic review and network meta-analysis of primary prevention trials
left.reason: The question matches (adults, vitamin C among supplements, death, heart disease, cancer), but this is only a protocol with no pooled results yet.

left.title: Reduced oxidative stress in STEMI patients treated by primary percutaneous coronary intervention and with antioxidant therapy: a systematic review
left.reason: Patients with heart attack undergoing PCI, treated with mixed antioxidant drugs, with oxidative stress and damage outcomes; a different question.

left.title: Effect of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on cardiovascular outcomes: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
left.reason: Placebo-controlled trials on cardiovascular events and death include vitamin C, but the abstract shows only pooled antioxidant vitamin results.

left.title: Do antioxidants prevent colorectal cancer? A meta-analysis
left.reason: Colorectal cancer and death outcomes vs placebo, but vitamin C is reported only combined with vitamin E, and some trials enrolled adenoma patients.

left.title: Does ascorbic acid protect against contrast-induced acute kidney injury in patients undergoing coronary angiography: a systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized, controlled trials
left.reason: The outcome is kidney injury from contrast dye in patients having coronary angiography.

left.title: Systematic review: primary and secondary prevention of gastrointestinal cancers with antioxidant supplements
left.reason: Placebo-controlled trials on gastrointestinal cancer and death include vitamin C, but the abstract shows only pooled antioxidant results.

left.title: Antioxidant supplements for preventing gastrointestinal cancers
left.reason: Placebo-controlled prevention trials on cancer and death that include vitamin C, but the abstract shows only pooled antioxidant results, not vitamin C apart.

left.title: The efficacy and safety of multivitamin and mineral supplement use to prevent cancer and chronic disease in adults: a systematic review for a National Institutes of Health state-of-the-science conference
left.reason: Adults and outcomes of cancer, heart disease and death match, but vitamin C is given only in multivitamin or mineral combinations.

left.title: Antioxidant supplements for preventing gastrointestinal cancers
left.reason: Placebo-controlled trials on gastrointestinal cancer and death include vitamin C, but the abstract gives no separate vitamin C result.

left.title: Antioxidant vitamins in the prevention of cardiovascular disease: a systematic review
left.reason: Covers antioxidant vitamins, including vitamin C, for heart disease prevention, but it is a mixed narrative review with no pooled vitamin C trial result.
